findings.evidence: Prologue: on the sinking Lusitania an agitated man says 'it must be a woman... women and children first' and gives an American girl an oilskin packet of 'vitally important papers'; Carter later names him Danvers and her Jane Finn
'Tommy, old thing!' 'Tuppence, old bean!' meet at Dover Street Tube; Tommy demobbed; Tuppence is 'fifth daughter of Archdeacon Cowley' and did hospital work
Both are short of money and jobs; 'Trading under the name of the Young Adventurers, Ltd.?'; they draft an advertisement for hire
Whittington says 'I happened to overhear part of your conversation' and offers £100 to enter Madame Colombier's pensionnat in Paris
Tuppence says 'Jane Finn' and Whittington turns 'purple with rage'; he gives her 'fifty to go on with'; next day the Esthonia Glassware office is closed; Tommy had overheard the name in the street
'there are only two answers!'
First letter signed 'A. CARTER'
Tommy: 'I recognized you at once. Saw you in France when I was with the Intelligence'
Carter explains the draft secret agreement 'implicates a number of our statesmen'; 'Bolshevist gold is pouring into this country to procure a Revolution'
'He is always spoken of by the unassuming title of "Mr. Brown."'
'a certain man, whose real name is unknown to us'
'How would you like to work for me?... Find Jane Finn'
Second letter signed 'JULIUS P. HERSHEIMMER'
Julius claims to be Jane's cousin; 'Inspector Brown' took the only photograph; afterwards 'All barriers went down' and they join forces
Tuppence reasons that Danvers was shadowed by a woman who may have been 'Rita' and checks the Lusitania survivor list
At 20 South Audley Mansions: 'Marguerite... She's mostly called that [Rita]'
Tommy follows Boris to a Soho house, copies the knock, says 'Mr. Brown?' and is let in
He overhears the meeting with Number One, later identified as Kramenin; the strike date is 'The 29th'
'A crashing blow descended on his head'; he later bargains: 'I believe that I can find them'
Albert, the lift-boy, arranges the job; Tuppence goes in as a house-parlourmaid
Mrs. Vandemeyer hires 'Prudence Cooper' as house-parlourmaid
'Sir James Peel Edgerton... the famous K.C.' calls at the flat
'a change does no harm sometimes... Just a hint'; he later helps them
Mrs. Vandemeyer holds a revolver to her: 'I'll shoot you like a dog'
Tuppence seizes the revolver and offers 'a hundred thousand' from her American millionaire friend
'Who is Mr. Brown?' 'Yes... I know'
She faints on seeing Sir James and Julius; they keep a vigil; by morning she is dead, with 'an odour of chloral'
Dr. Hall: 'Janet Vandemeyer' suffers 'complete loss of memory' and 'is no longer under my care'
Julius proposes and says 'think it over until to-morrow'; Tuppence weeps 'I do love you so' over Tommy's photo; her note says 'Let's leave it till then'
Telegram: 'Come at once, Moat House, Ebury, Yorkshire... TOMMY'
Annette slips him a penknife, helps him escape and cries 'To Marguerite!'; at the Ritz he is told Miss Cowley has gone out
After a week at Ebury they are 'no nearer to discovering Tuppence's whereabouts'
Telegram: 'Jane Finn found. Come Manchester... PEEL EDGERTON'; at the Holyhead cliff path the packet reads 'WITH THE COMPLIMENTS OF MR. BROWN'
findings.note: The message appears in sympathetic ink rather than plain ink; this is minor and not a distortion

findings.evidence: Her clothes are 'Washed up on the Yorkshire coast'; Tommy rages at Julius: 'I loved her'
Annette's photograph is in Julius's drawer; his letter to Carter says 'that girl at Manchester was just a plant'
Tommy: 'I kept my mind open between the two of them'
He leaves Julius a note about the Argentine and lets Sir James see his letter; the original wire reveals Astley Priors, Gatehouse, Kent
'She'd never spell her name "Twopence"... Julius had seen it... but Sir James hadn't!'
Julius holds Kramenin at gunpoint and makes him fetch both girls; Jane admits she has been 'fooling them all the time' for 'Five long years'
Tommy sends the girls to Sir James: 'I was sure they'd fetch up at the house in Soho'; the papers are behind the picture of 'Marguerite with her casket of jewels'
Jane takes the treaty from behind the picture; Sir James says 'I am Mr. Brown'
He raises an automatic and is 'seized from behind'; Tommy and Julius had hidden behind the curtain in the recess
He raises 'the hand which bore the big signet ring' to his lips and dies amid 'an odour of bitter almonds'
'Deprived of their chief, the organization fell to pieces'; the treaty is 'reduced to ashes'; 'It was to be Peace'
At the Savoy supper Carter reads from the brown diary, Sir William accepts Tommy ('You're my heir'), and Jane is toasted
Julius proposes to Jane and she says 'I love you now, Julius'; in a taxi Tommy says 'You won't be able to get out of marrying me'
'Marriage is called a haven... But do you know what I think it is?... A sport!'; Carter's diary entry notes the boy is 'hard to blind... to facts'
